Author Google Docs and Slides decks as artifacts, then publish with the Google connector. Revise one published from an artifact by editing that artifact and publishing again, never through the cloud API. An uploaded deck has no editable text; agree that first if they need to edit it in Slides. Write and format a Google Sheet through the Sheets connector.
document: an editable written deliverable (docx). pdf: a fixed-layout document. presentation: a slide deck (pptx by default). spreadsheet: a workbook, table, or CSV data export (xlsx by default). markdown: a plain markdown file (md); only when the user asked for markdown or a .md file. other: any other plain file deliverable (txt, ics, json, srt, ...); name its extension in output_formats.Short, neutral name shown to the user. Use the literal artifact category or supplied name from `verbatim_request`. If the current request is anaphoric, such as "Yes, build that", use the literal category or name from the exact prior user quote or explicitly accepted assistant proposal it refers to. Otherwise do not derive the name from preferences or facts. Do not invent a product concept, audience, mood, positioning, benefit, or aesthetic. Example: "Make me a trip planner" becomes `Trip Planner`, not `Kyoto Slow Days`.

On a turn driven by a literal user message, copy the user's message exactly. If that message answers a clarifying question you asked about their earlier build request, copy that request and then their whole message on a new line, each word for word. On a producer turn (scheduler, feed, workflow, or subagent work), copy the exact originating build instruction; when that instruction is embedded in a larger packet, copy only its explicitly labeled requested outcome and instructions, excluding activation text, titles, summaries, ids, prerequisites, and wrapper text. This field is authoritative for the current requested scope: the builder reads it as the requester's own words, so anything you add becomes a fabricated requirement. Add nothing else: no summary, no other conversation, nothing of your own; the builder gathers and validates its own sources, images included.
The exact goal ID, when this deliverable is a document for an existing goal; omit it otherwise. Set it and the file is built inside that goal's folder, so it is one of that goal's documents from the moment it exists. Leave it out and the file is built in the shared artifacts area. Do not move or copy a file between the two afterwards: pick the destination here. A slug names one file artifact across both places, so pick a slug no existing document uses; scope a goal document's slug to its goal (`board-prep-q3-report`) when a plain one might already exist. A slug that already names a built document in the other place is refused, and nothing is built.
output_formatsOnly for an explicitly requested container. document: docx. pdf: pdf. presentation: pptx, pdf, or html. spreadsheet: xlsx or csv. Omit otherwise; each kind renders its canonical container. Required for kind other: the deliverable's file extension(s). To change an existing artifact use artifact.edit. To author a Google Doc or Slides deck, build it here and publish with the Google connector. Create and edit Google Sheets through the Sheets connector.
Build a hosted page whose content is fixed at build and saves nothing a visitor enters. A static page runs client-side JavaScript, maps, and any CSS framework; it resets on reload and is the only kind that can be exported. A page rendering data the user already provided, with no ongoing entry and no refresh, is static with the data embedded. Anything it must do at use time beyond the browser (save entries, fetch current or account data, run a model) needs the fullstack kind, as does content that goes stale, or is reshuffled on a schedule, unless the user asked for a one-time result or declined a refresh.

Before creating, consider whether the request means changing an existing artifact instead. When the page's content depends on data you do not have (schedules, rosters, menus, personal content), ask the user for it before building rather than filling in invented stand-ins.

Pass the user's exact ask in `verbatim_request`, a display `name`, and a factual `icon_subject` describing the artifact's subject and purpose.
A static page is shareable as a public link: everyone with the link opens the same page, each visitor runs it alone, and nothing one visitor enters is saved or visible to anyone else. The fullstack kind that saves entries has no public link, so when a request needs both, name the choice (a page anyone can open, or a private app that saves their entries) and create nothing until they pick. When the request implies people writing together or seeing each other's changes, say so plainly rather than presenting the page as shared or approximating sharing with a workaround.
Short, neutral name shown to the user; it sets the slug. Use the literal artifact category or supplied name from `verbatim_request`. If the current request is anaphoric, such as "Yes, build that", use the literal category or name from the exact prior user quote or explicitly accepted assistant proposal it refers to. Otherwise do not derive the name from preferences or facts. Do not invent a product concept, audience, mood, positioning, benefit, or aesthetic. Example: "Make me a trip planner" becomes `Trip Planner`, not `Kyoto Slow Days`.
Describe what the artifact is about and what it lets the user do in one or two plain sentences. Ground this in the user's request or explicitly accepted context. Start with the main subject and purpose. `icon_subject` is factual topic context for automatic icon selection, not a requested depiction or an icon name. Keep it separate from the builder's instructions in `verbatim_request`; do not add requirements, suggest an icon, or describe visual styling. Example: "A concert-date tracker for the rock band Train."
The exact goal ID, supplied when this new artifact directly supports an existing goal; optional otherwise. After the build succeeds, the runtime attempts to link it. Omit this for unrelated artifacts, and confirm the artifact appears in the matching read tool (`user_goal.get` or `tracking.get`) before claiming the link exists.
Optional, web artifacts only. The research directory from finished deep research (the `Research directory:` path in its handoff, under the workspace's research_notes folder, holding report.md), whose values the builder embeds with their sources and researches beyond only where they stop. The builder reads the folder itself; keep `verbatim_request` as the user's exact words.A visual template for the web artifact. Set it only when the user asks to use a template by name, such as "use the muse template"; never infer one from a look they describe.

Before calling the tool, declare every connector method clearly required by the user's workflow; do not defer known connector needs to the builder. To change an existing artifact use artifact.edit.
Build a hosted web app with a storage/server layer when the experience calls for saved state, live or refreshed data, or data from the app that you need to retrieve and use. Choose based on the intended workflow, even if the user hasn't specified storage or backend requirements.

Before creating around a connected account or live source, check the source is available. If it isn't, surface that before creating: tell the user now and let them choose to connect it, provide the data, or start it empty. Create with an empty state only on their explicit choice, and never describe a stub integration or seeded stand-in as pulling real data.

A fullstack app runs privately for this user and has no public link. When the request involves sharing the app or other people using it, say so before building and let them decide.
Add a trigger whenever the artifact should record or update data on a schedule without the user asking each time: content that goes stale or is reshuffled, or records it keeps in sync. Add one for each schedule the user asked for; if they named none, add one daily trigger without asking first and tell them, unless they declined a refresh. Omit it when the artifact needs no refresh.

reason.description: Optional label for needs_input or blocked. Omit for completed or when no label fits; explain the situation in summary. For needs_input, use sign_in, verification_code, captcha, payment, approval, missing_information, decision, or other, or personal_agent_protocol when you stop because the site supports the Personal Agent Protocol. Payment means missing payment details or a payment choice; approval means permission for something outside the assignment, not the separate purchase approval. Use captcha only for an unsolved puzzle when the user can take over this browser and no other site will do. For blocked, use bot_wall, captcha_unsolved, ai_agent_refused, ip_blocked, rate_limited, sign_in_required, sign_in_rejected, not_available, site_error, site_unreachable, approval_denied, browser_failure, or order_unconfirmed. Use order_unconfirmed when the merchant's outcome remains unresolved after permitted verification and no user input can resolve it.
